Apps that collect API tokens or instruct customers to create individual 3LO apps don't comply with our [Security requirements for cloud apps](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/marketplace/security-requirements/) and [Acceptable use policy](https://www.atlassian.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy#wrongful-activities).

OAuth 2.0 (3LO) involves three parties:
- An Atlassian site (*resource*)
- A user (*resource owner*)
- An external application/service (*client*).
For example, a Jira or Confluence site (*resource*), an Atlassian user (*resource owner*), and Gmail (*client*). Underlying the authorization interactions between these three parties is an authorization server.

results.title: Basic auth for REST APIs
results.snippet:
This page shows you how REST clients can authenticate themselves using **[basic authentication](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication)** with an [Atlassian account](https://confluence.atlassian.com/cloud/atlassian-account-for-users-873871199.html) email address and [API token](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/Vo71Nw). Authentication using passwords has been deprecated.

Basic auth requires API tokens. You generate an API token for your Atlassian account and use it to authenticate anywhere where you would have used a password. This enhances security because:
- you're not saving your primary account password outside of where you authenticate
- you can quickly revoke individual API tokens on a per-use basis
- API tokens will allow you to authenticate even if your Atlassian Cloud organization has two-factor authentication or SAML enabled.
See the Atlassian Cloud Support [API tokens](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/Vo71Nw) article to discover how to generate an API token.

To create an issue, you will need to know certain key metadata, like the ID of the project that the issue will be created in, or the ID of the issue type. You can request the create metadata for all issue types across all projects by using the `createmeta` resource.

The Atlassian Rovo MCP Server is a cloud-hosted [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) server that connects AI-powered clients to your Atlassian Cloud apps. It provides a standardized interface for AI assistants, IDEs, and automation tools to read, create, and update work across Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Bitbucket, Loom, and the wider Atlassian platform - all secured by OAuth 2.1 authorization and your existing Atlassian permissions.
## What you can do
With the Atlassian Rovo MCP Server, AI clients can:
- **Search and summarize** Jira work items, Confluence pages, Bitbucket pull requests, and other Atlassian content without context switching.
- **Retrieve Loom recordings**, including transcripts, comments, AI briefs, and extracted meeting action items.
- **Create and update** work items, pages, and other content using natural language commands.
- **Automate repetitive work**, such as generating Jira work items from meeting notes or creating Confluence documentation from specs.
- **Query across apps** using Teamwork Graph, such as finding the pull requests, deployments, and documents connected to a work item.

The Atlassian Rovo MCP Server is adding six new Jira Align tools through MCP V2 across two new toolsets: `read_jira_align` and `write_jira_align`. These tools enable AI agents and workflows to interact directly with Jira Align data for portfolio reporting, planning rollups, terminology discovery, and backlog hygiene.

- Write tools belong to the `write_jira_align` toolset and require the `write:jira-align:agent-interface` scope.

results.snippet:
Atlassian MCP Server is a cloud-hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives your AI tools secure, real-time access to your data across Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, and other Atlassian apps.
Connect Atlassian MCP and your AI clients like Claude, Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT, and others to securely access and interact with your Atlassian data. By connecting Atlassian’s MCP server, you can bring the context of your Jira issues, Confluence pages, and Teamwork Graph directly into your preferred AI development tools and chat interfaces.
## How Rovo credit usage works with Atlassian MCP
When an AI client calls via Atlassian MCP to retrieve data or generate insights, it consumes Rovo credits. These credits come from the same shared pool used by Rovo Chat, Studio, Agents, and the Teamwork Graph, across your organization.

Enriched Teamwork Graph (TWG) API and tool calls, including unified search and context tools called via [Atlassian MCP](https://support.atlassian.com/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server/docs/use-atlassian-rovo-mcp-server/), consume Rovo credits. These include but are not limited to: `getTeamworkGraphContext`,`twg rovo search`, `searchAtlassian`, `search`.
